newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moderate quake shakes east Japan, no damage seen.
newsitem.headline: Moderate quake shakes east Japan, no damage seen.

text.p: A moderately strong earthquake rattled eastern Japan on Tuesday and shook buildings in Tokyo, but there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties, Japan's Meteorological Agency said.

The agency said the quake, with a magnitude of 5.5 on the Richter scale, was centred in the sea off the Boso peninsula east of Tokyo at a depth of about 50 km (30 miles). It struck at around 4.40 p.m. (0700 GMT).
A quake of five on the Richter scale can be powerful enough to cause damage and injury if it strikes a built-up area.
The quake was most strongly felt in parts of Chiba prefecture, just to the east of the capital, but also caused buildings in Tokyo to sway.
The earthquake was four on the Japanese scale of seven -- a moderately strong tremor -- in Chiba and two in Tokyo.
The agency said there was no danger of the earthquake triggering tidal waves, known as tsunami in Japan.
